title: Sequential Spinodal Decompositions and Ordering Reactions in an As-Quenched Cr<sub>39</sub>Co<sub>18</sub>Fe<sub>18</sub>Ni<sub>18</sub>Al<sub>7</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 equiatomic (or near-equiatomic) high-entropy alloy synthesized as a single bcc solid-solution ingot
recollection.intervention: water-quench from the high-temperature bcc phase followed by isothermal aging (≈600-700 °C) and characterization by atom-probe tomography, synchrotron X-ray and TEM
recollection.structure: initial single-phase bcc solid solution that undergoes nanoscale compositional modulations (spinodal decomposition) into Cr-rich and (Co,Fe,Ni,Al)-rich bcc regions; subsequent ordering inside the (Co,Fe,Ni,Al)-rich zones produces coherent B2 or L12 ordered precipitates within the bcc matrix
recollection.mechanism: sequential spinodal decomposition driven by a miscibility gap in the multicomponent bcc phase, creating wavelength-≈3-5 nm composition waves, followed by vacancy-assisted diffusion that allows Al-rich regions to order (B2/L12), leading to strengthening
recollection.results: APT shows ~20–25 at.% amplitude in Cr concentration between spinodal peaks; ordered precipitates reach ~10 nm after 10 h aging; hardness rises from ~200 HV in the as-quenched state to ~550 HV after aging; yield strength increases above 1 GPa while maintaining ~10–15 % tensile ductility

score.note: The recalled heat treatment and characterization route are incorrect: the study annealed at 1100–1300 °C and water-quenched, rather than aging at 600–700 °C. The recollection partially captures BCC spinodal partitioning and subsequent B2 ordering, but misses the reciprocal hierarchical BCC/B2 nanoparticle structure and incorrectly suggests L12. Its core miscibility-gap/sequential-decomposition and Ni–Al-ordering mechanism is correct, although vacancy assistance and the stated wavelength are unsupported. All reported hardness, aging-time, strength, ductility, and feature-size values differ from the paper.
